correctness.rationale: All definitions, ambient Euclidean normalization, integer ranges, cap halfspace constraints and equality cases are explicit. The projection normal inequality certifies the unique capped-sum minimizer; convexity and symmetry yield the global Hausdorff maximum. A strict variance identity for mixed residuals characterizes every farthest face; the face dimensions/count and disjointness follow from ordered residual plateaus. Separate Riemann-sum analysis yields the two limiting branches and endpoint case; analytic differentiation gives one-sided third derivatives -2 and 0. Reproducible rational and independent quadratic-programming checks corroborate but do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: Canonical two-level orbit coarsening is an intrinsically motivated approximation of the standard permutahedron with fixed coordinate sum and full coordinate symmetry. The complete extremal set is a large collection of positive-dimensional faces rather than merely vertices; its limiting dimension saturates sharply at quarter density. The error has a genuine C2/non-C3 transition at exactly the same geometrically explained threshold. These are new structural quantitative conclusions beyond routine per-point capped-simplex projection.
